name: OpenShell
description: OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for autonomous AI agents.
one_liner: A safety cage for AI agents: it lets an agent read files, use passwords, and call outside services, but only the exact things you've approved — so a bug or a trick can't make it leak your data.
buyer: A security or platform engineering lead at a mid-size company rolling out AI coding or ops agents who must prove to IT/compliance that agents can't exfiltrate secrets or touch unapproved systems.
business_use_cases: An IT department running dozens of AI agents across engineering enforces 'this agent can only touch this repo and these three APIs,' satisfying a SOC 2 audit requirement.
A fintech company lets agents call internal banking APIs for automation, trusting the policy layer to block any attempt to reach an unapproved endpoint with real credentials.
A managed-IT provider offers 'agent governance as a service' to clients whose security team has blocked AI coding assistants, using this as the enforcement layer.

money_ideas.idea: Sell a hosted, managed gateway with audit dashboards and compliance reports to companies that don't want to run the infrastructure themselves.
Offer paid policy-writing and compliance-audit consulting for enterprises adopting AI agents.

steal_this: This weekend, run the quickstart, write one real policy file for an actual client's AI agent setup, and pitch 'lock down your AI agents in an afternoon' as a fixed-price service.
